claim: The Waterside Inn holds Three Stars in the 2026 MICHELIN Guide United Kingdom.
quote: Waterside Inn is a Three Stars: Exceptional cuisine restaurant in the 2026 MICHELIN Guide United Kingdom.

claim: The Fat Duck holds Three Stars in the 2026 MICHELIN Guide United Kingdom.
quote: The Fat Duck is a Three Stars: Exceptional cuisine restaurant in the 2026 MICHELIN Guide United Kingdom.

claim: Bray's Michelin-starred venues all retained their stars in the 2026 guide; The Hinds Head (1 star) is the village's only other starred restaurant, and no Bray restaurant holds two stars.
quote: The Waterside Inn in Bray has retained its coveted three Michelin stars, and The Fat Duck on the High Street has retained its three Michelin stars, while nearby pub The Hinds Head continues to hold one Michelin star.

claim: Bray contains two of the eight three-Michelin-starred restaurants in the United Kingdom, in a village of roughly 9,100 residents about 5 miles from Windsor.
quote: Bray contains two of the eight three-Michelin-starred restaurants in the United Kingdom.

claim: The Waterside Inn opened in 1972, was awarded its first Michelin star in 1974 and its third in 1985, and has held three stars continuously since.
quote: In 1985 the restaurant gained its third Michelin star, which it has retained ever since.

claim: Waterside Inn marked 40 consecutive years of three MICHELIN Stars in 2025 — the longest run outside France.
quote: The Waterside Inn celebrates 40 years with three MICHELIN Stars.

claim: Alain Roux is chef-patron of the Waterside Inn on Ferry Road, Bray, serving classical French cuisine in a riverside restaurant-with-rooms.
quote: Classical French cuisine emphasizing extraordinary sauces to beautifully composed desserts.

claim: Waterside Inn pricing (2023): seven-course tasting menu £235, four-course dinner menu £160 (£140 at lunch), plus a full à la carte.
quote: a tasting menu at £235, a four-course menu at £160 at dinner (£140 at lunch) as well as a full a la carte menu.

claim: The Fat Duck opened on 16 August 1995 in a 16th-century building in Bray, gained its third Michelin star in 2004, briefly lost all stars during a 2016 renovation, and regained them in 2017.
quote: Opened on 16 August 1995... became the third UK restaurant to achieve three Michelin stars in 2004... lost the stars in 2016 during renovation and regained all three in 2017.

claim: The Fat Duck is Heston Blumenthal's three-Michelin-starred restaurant at High Street, Bray, Berkshire SL6 2AQ.
quote: three-Michelin-star perfection... unexpected flavour pairings, playful innovation and unique culinary creations.

claim: The Fat Duck opens Wed–Sun for dinner and Fri–Sun for lunch, charges £285–£365 per person for food, recommends smart casual, and forfeits prepayment if cancelled within 7 days.
quote: Wednesday to Sunday for dinner (starting 18:00) and Friday to Sunday for lunch (starting 12:00). The restaurant is closed Monday and Tuesday. Menus range from £285–£365 per person.

claim: Snail Porridge and Sound of the Sea are among the iconic dishes that defined the Fat Duck's three-star tasting menu.
quote: iconic, thought-provoking dishes like Snail Porridge and Sound of the Sea.

claim: The 2026 MICHELIN Guide for Great Britain & Ireland was unveiled at a ceremony in Dublin on 9 February 2026.
quote: The MICHELIN Guide Ceremony for Great Britain & Ireland 2026... 6pm on Monday 9th February at the Convention Centre in Dublin.

claim: Bray is the only village in the UK with two three-Michelin-star restaurants; the UK currently has eight three-star restaurants overall in the 2026 guide.
quote: Bray is home to two of the UK's three-Michelin-starred restaurants — The Fat Duck and the Waterside Inn.

claim: The nearest two-Michelin-star restaurant to Bray is Tom Kerridge's The Hand and Flowers in Marlow, ~7 miles north, the UK's first two-star pub.
quote: The Hand and Flowers is a pub and restaurant in Marlow, Buckinghamshire... the first pub to ever achieve two Michelin stars.

claim: The Hinds Head, Heston Blumenthal's pub on Bray's High Street, holds one Michelin star — not two or three.
quote: The Hinds Head, Bray... one Michelin star.
